assigned.title: Series navigation and the next episode
assigned.acceptance: A viewer can move through a series without going back to the catalog. Today every season of a series renders as one flat stack on the title page, with no season selector, no per-episode progress and no way to reach the next episode. REQUIRED: season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place. REQUIRED: per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API. REQUIRED: a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place. REQUIRED: the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a component, because 'what plays next' is exactly the kind of decision this project requires to be reconstructible.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

typecheck.evidence: Re-recorded at 5dad6d3575f990a650600256096ead7334913435, superseding the aa80fac evidence: this round changed demo-title-details.ts and added an e2e spec, so the earlier result describes a tree that no longer exists. npx tsc --noEmit in apps/web: exit 0. cd e2e && npx tsc --noEmit: exit 0, which matters because series-navigation.spec.ts is new and imports DEMO from src/fixtures rather than src/env -- the compiler caught that on the first attempt.

unit.evidence: npx vitest run in apps/web at 5dad6d3575f990a650600256096ead7334913435: 84 files / 1494 tests, exit 0. Six new cases in demo-title-details.test.ts run the REAL decision over the REAL catalog rather than over fixtures the test built for itself -- northstar has two seasons that still sum to its advertised episodeCount, episodes are numbered within their season, runtime is derived from the ordinal in the series so season 2 episode 1 is not a byte copy of season 1 episode 1, resolveNextEpisode crosses the boundary from northstar-s1e5 to northstar-s2e1, it ends the series at northstar-s2e3 rather than wrapping, and harbor-lights stays single-season with harbor-lights-s1e6's rights still null. NON-VACUITY, each reverted after measuring: collapsing northstar's layout back to [8] fails 4 of the 6; a layout of [5,2] fails all of them with the invariant's own message, 'the season layout for northstar covers 7 episodes but its catalog entry advertises 8'. lint: 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in PW-0313's surface, untouched).

e2e.evidence: Playwright 1.62.1, chromium revision 1234, retries 0, at 5dad6d3575f990a650600256096ead7334913435. THE FIRST BROWSER COVERAGE THIS TASK HAS EVER HAD, and the reason it could not exist before is recorded in the spec: every demo series had one season, so a tab strip with one tab was all any build could show. e2e/tests/series-navigation.spec.ts, 6 cases, 18/18 over --repeat-each=3 in development. It proves two tabs, different episodes behind each (5 and 3, summing to the advertised 8), mouse switching both ways, and the keyboard -- roving tabindex, ArrowRight, Home and End with automatic activation, which is the first keyboard interaction in this application with a test behind it. Two assertions are about absence: a one-season series gets NO tablist rather than a hidden one, and the closed season is absent from the ACCESSIBILITY TREE, which is what distinguishes hidden from styling a panel away. WHOLE PROJECTS, three configurations, all exit 0: development chromium+api 93 passed / 14 skipped; production no database 61 passed / 46 skipped; production + real PostgreSQL 16.15 at postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl, 8 tables asserted, 76 passed / 31 skipped. series-navigation skips outside development because those builds serve no catalog metadata, which is the existing convention and the reason the skip count rises. THREE CORRECTIONS THE BROWSER MADE, every one of them the test being wrong rather than the product: getByRole does not see a hidden subtree; a single-season series renders the flat stack and has no season-panel testid at all; and a bare link count gave 11 for 6 episodes because each card carries a title link, so play affordances are counted by accessible name. WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER: clause 3, the end-of-playback next-episode affordance, is UNBUILT -- it lives in player-surface.tsx, which the round-103 ruling puts out of bounds until PW-0306 completes. PW-0307 stays IN_PROGRESS. UNVERIFIED: Linux chromium in a container; no Windows runtime, no WebView2, no attended GUI behaviour is claimed.
